claim: ARIA learns when an executor model should consult a stronger advisor on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and tau2-bench, and includes a rate-matched Random placement arm but no oracle arm and no elicited-confidence or probe signal.
stance_target: L3 routing by elicited or probe confidence with random and oracle arms is NARROW (not OCCUPIED)
scope_conditions: Agentic workflows, one executor-advisor model pair, Magentic-One framework; routes to a stronger model, not to execution budget
quoted_support: A Random-placement control approximates ARIA's consultation rate to separate the effect of consultation timing from simply having advisor access.
numbers: recovers 44-81% of the executor-advisor success gap
less than half the advisor model's cost

breadth.confidence_families: not present as a readout: signal is workflow-level state, explicitly not self-assessment or internal confidence (Related Work, State representation); a prompted LLM-decided consultation baseline in Table 1
breadth.label_source: task success of the agentic run
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (searched: ECE, AUROC, Brier, calibrat); success-cost trade-off only
breadth.granularity: consultation decision at workflow contact points (Table 1)

claim: The ARIA design deliberately avoids model-internal confidence or self-assessment because their reliability is limited, so it does not test confidence-routed budgets.
stance_target: L3 routing by elicited or probe confidence is NARROW
quoted_support: The representation is intentionally based on workflow-level signals rather than model-internal confidence or self-assessment, whose reliability is known to be limited
